calls.head: Cole and Vlasic get the Suzuki assignment
calls.body: At home, the Blackhawks keep sending Cole and Vlasic out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jeff Blashill has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Canadiens’ first line is Caufield, Suzuki and Slafkovský.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Cole plays his 1,000th game, but the Blackhawks lose
paras: Connor Bedard opened the scoring for the Blackhawks early in the first, but that’s where Chicago’s luck ran out. Jake Evans made it 1-1 for Montréal late in the period, and he struck again shorthanded midway through the second to put the Canadiens ahead 2-1. Kaiden Guhle stretched the lead to 3-1 late in the period. Mike Matheson added an empty-net goal with less than three minutes left to make it 4-1. Evans added an assist for a three-point night.
The chances were closer than the score. Jacob Fowler made 20 saves for the Canadiens, and Spencer Knight stopped 24 of 27.
Neither power play scored: the Canadiens killed all five Blackhawks power plays, and the Blackhawks killed all three of Montréal’s. The Habs moved to 5-3-2, and the Blackhawks dropped to 3-7-0.

items.text: Cole Caufield had a point in all six of his games against Chicago since 2023-24, and that run ended.
Connor Bedard has a point in all six of his games against Montréal since 2023-24.
The Blackhawks’ Ian Cole played his 1,000th NHL game.
Mike Matheson scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 31 (twelve games played since).
